fields.meta_title: One Page Website Builder With a Working Form | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a one page website from one prompt: sections in scroll order and a form that saves every inquiry to your database. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a One Page Website With a Form That Works
fields.hero_description: Describe the business and the sections it needs. Emergent builds the one page website in one pass, with a contact form that works on the day it goes live.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a One Page Website Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: What a visitor scrolls through, and what happens to the inquiry they leave at the end.
fields.feature_1:
Sections in the order visitors scroll

Emergent lays out the intro, services, reviews and contact sections in the order your prompt lists them. Each one opens on its own heading, for visitors who skim on a phone.
fields.feature_2:
Menu links that jump down the page

Every section gets an anchor, and each header link scrolls to its section. Ask for a pinned header and it stays in view on a phone, with the menu folded into one button.
fields.feature_3:
Every inquiry saved as a row

Inquiries are saved to a database you own, one row per submission. The columns match the fields your prompt names: ask the form for a budget and every row arrives with one.
fields.feature_4:
Edits made by message, not by dragging

Send a message such as "move reviews above pricing" or "add a second phone number to the footer," and Emergent rewrites that part of the code. Nothing is dragged into place.
fields.feature_5:
Live on a domain with your name on it

A custom domain puts your business name in the address bar, not a builder's subdomain. Print it on your business cards and invoices; it is the address customers type.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Nothing stays locked in Emergent. Export the full code, contact form included, to your GitHub repository, where a developer can host it on their own server or extend it.

fields.usecase_heading: One Page Websites for Four Trades
fields.tab_content_1:
Portfolio first, inquiry form last, one scroll

Dana Reyes shoots products and portraits for small brands. Her page opens on a grid of recent shoots and ends with an inquiry form asking for the shoot date and budget, with her packages in between. Each inquiry is saved to a table, and any budget of $2,500 or more posts to her Slack.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every quote request checked against the service area

Plumbing calls come from the towns Harbor Lane Plumbing covers, and a few from places it does not. The page puts the phone number in the header and a quote form at the bottom. Requests from a town outside the service area are tagged Out of area before anyone calls back.
fields.tab_content_3:
Large parties go to the events manager

The reservation form sits under Juniper Table's menu. Parties of 8 or fewer go straight into the bookings table. A request for 10 guests skips the table: Lena, the events manager, gets it by email with the party size and the requested time.
fields.tab_content_4:
When the race fills, signups become a waitlist

At 400 runners, the Riverside 5K page stops taking registrations. The course map and race-morning schedule stay up, and the signup button opens a waitlist form instead. Each entry gets a numbered spot and a confirmation email with that number.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a One Page Website
fields.howto_description: Plan the sections and the form before you write the prompt. Decide what the form asks first: it is where the page earns its keep.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Check that one page is enough
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the sections in scroll order
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: A one-page site fits a business with one offer and one action a visitor should take, such as booking a table or asking for a quote. If you sell unrelated services to different buyers, give each of them a page of its own.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the sections down in the order a visitor needs them: what you do, proof that you do it well, what it costs, how to reach you. Cut any section that repeats another, and keep the contact form as the last stop.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the business, the sections and the details only you know: phone number, service towns, package prices, opening hours. Emergent builds the first version from that prompt. The more specific the details, the less copy you rewrite afterward.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each section a short name a visitor would look for, such as Services or Book, and use the same word in the menu. Four or five links fit on a phone screen; leave the rest out of the menu.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the fields the form asks for and what happens to each entry: a row in your database, an email to you, a Slack post for the large jobs. Ask only for fields you will use when you reply to someone.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the scroll on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on your own phone and scroll it end to end. Tap every menu link, submit the form once and confirm the entry landed where you asked. Then read it again with your phone's text size turned up.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page and connect the domain you bought. Then put the link wherever customers already look for you: your Google Business Profile and Instagram bio first, then the email signature on every reply you send.

plan.angle: The top 10 is galleries (One Page Love, Awwwards, Made in Webflow), template shops (Nicepage, Etsy, Webflow templates) and builder blogs (Wix, Squarespace, Framer). They show what a one-pager looks like; none shows what happens after a visitor fills in its form. This page wins by covering when one page is enough, the sections in scroll order, and four real businesses whose one action (inquire, request a quote, reserve, register) lands in a database the owner keeps, with Emergent as the builder that hands over the code.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a One Page Website With a Form That Works' and hero ('menu links that jump to each section, plus a form that saves to a database you own') cover the whole page, not one feature.

intent.evidence: Example-led SERP (One Page Love, Awwwards, builder example roundups): four worked one-page sites in the tabs, when one page is enough (howto_step_1), sections in scroll order, and 8 PAA questions answered.

specificity.evidence: Small-business detail throughout: 'Harbor Lane Plumbing', 'Out of area', 'Parties of 8 or fewer', 'At 400 runners', 'your Google Business Profile and Instagram bio first'.

openers.evidence: Two FAQ answers open on fragments (CONTENT_DEFECTS #2): FAQ 5 'Static hosting on a free service.'; FAQ 10 'A photographer's portfolio with an inquiry form, a plumber's page that checks the service area, a restaurant menu with reservations, a race page with registration.'

craft.evidence: Ideas restated across fields (CONTENT_DEFECTS #21): editing by message (features_subheading, feature_1, feature_4, FAQ 2, howto_step_6), menu links jump to sections (hero, feature_2, howto_step_4, FAQ 1), free tier plus domain in credits (feature_5, FAQ 3, FAQ 4), one action per page (howto_description, howto_step_1, FAQ 6, FAQ 10), entries to Slack or email (feature_3, howto_step_5).

voice.evidence: Summary sentences that restate the one before (HUB_RULES 2b): FAQ 5 'A page with an inquiry form needs somewhere to keep what visitors send.'; FAQ 3 'That makes a free one page website a real option.'

truth.evidence: FAQ 4 'The cost that recurs is the domain name' (untrue as a general statement; hosting plans recur); FAQ 8 'The legal question most site owners meet is copyright.' (unsupported generalization); FAQ 7 'Hosting the page and storing what its form collects are left to you.' (unsourced third-party claim).

distinct.evidence: Own page: portfolio, plumber, restaurant, 5K race; splash-page and thank-you-page siblings are linked, not imitated; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: FAQ 10 replays the four tab stories as its answer (CONTENT_DEFECTS #18, #21): 'A photographer's portfolio with an inquiry form, a plumber's page that checks the service area, a restaurant menu with reservations, a race page with registration.'

images.evidence: Each tab matches its copy: $2,500 Slack threshold with a $3,000 inquiry; Benson tagged Out of area; 10 guests sent to Lena; 400 of 400 spots and waitlist spots 11 and 12 with confirmation emailed; reserved domain danareyes.example.

findings.quote: Building the page can cost nothing on a free tier. The cost that recurs is the domain name
findings.issue: Stated as a general fact about one-page websites, which is untrue: most hosted builders bill a recurring plan, and the page's own feature_5 and FAQ 3 say a custom domain on Emergent is billed in credits. Only the registration-and-renewal point is sourced (ICANN). Same class: FAQ 8 'The legal question most site owners meet is copyright.' (an unsourced claim about what most owners meet); FAQ 4 'Hiring a designer or buying a premium one page website theme adds a one-time fee.' (unsourced; design retainers recur).
findings.fix: FAQ 4: 'Building it can cost nothing on a free tier. Expect to renew the domain name with your registrar each term; a hosted plan or a designer adds to that.' FAQ 8: open on the sourced Copyright Office point without 'most site owners'.

findings.quote: Hosting the page and storing what its form collects are left to you.
findings.issue: A claim about a third-party system that the recorded OpenAI source (writing and code blocks, preview) does not cover.
findings.fix: Source it, or drop the sentence and let the Emergent sentence carry the contrast: 'Emergent also publishes the page, connects the domain and saves entries to a database you own.'

findings.quote: A form that stores entries needs a backend, which static hosting does not provide. A page with an inquiry form needs somewhere to keep what visitors send.
findings.issue: The second sentence restates the first (a summary sentence). Same class in FAQ 3: 'That makes a free one page website a real option.' restates 'its free tier covers building and publishing the page'.
findings.fix: Cut both restating sentences; if FAQ 3 needs a secondary, place 'free one page website' in a sentence that adds a fact.

findings.quote: Static hosting on a free service.
findings.issue: The answer opens on a fragment. Same class in FAQ 10: 'A photographer's portfolio with an inquiry form, a plumber's page that checks the service area, a restaurant menu with reservations, a race page with registration.'
findings.fix: Open each with a full sentence: 'The cheapest way is static hosting on a free service such as GitHub Pages.'

findings.quote: A photographer's portfolio with an inquiry form, a plumber's page that checks the service area, a restaurant menu with reservations, a race page with registration.
findings.issue: FAQ 10 restates the four tab stories (tab_content_1 to 4) instead of adding ideas.
findings.fix: Give ideas the tabs do not cover (an event venue, a wedding RSVP page, a book launch, a clinic's booking page), each with its one action.

findings.quote: Send a message such as "move reviews above pricing" or "add a second phone number to the footer," and Emergent rewrites that part of the code.
findings.issue: Editing by message is said five times: features_subheading 'each one changes with a follow-up message'; feature_1 'Adding a section later means naming it and saying where it should sit.'; feature_4 (quoted); FAQ 2 'Each change after that is another message.'; howto_step_6_des 'Describe anything awkward in a message and Emergent fixes it.'
findings.fix: Keep it in feature_4; let the other fields say something new (feature_1 on section order; FAQ 2 on what a beginner must decide; howto_step_6 on what to check).

findings.quote: Every section gets an anchor, and each header link scrolls to its section.
findings.issue: Menu links jumping to sections is restated in hero 'menu links that jump to each section', howto_step_4_des 'Ask for a header menu whose links jump to each section', FAQ 1 'Links in the menu jump down to a section instead of loading a new page.'
findings.fix: Feature_2 owns it; howto_step_4 keeps only its new advice (short section names, four or five links); FAQ 1 defines the term without the menu mechanics.

findings.quote: Your page goes live on a custom domain, which Emergent includes and bills in credits. Publishing also works on the free tier
findings.issue: Restated in FAQ 3 'its free tier covers building and publishing the page ... Connecting your own domain is included as well and is paid for in credits.' and FAQ 4 'Building the page can cost nothing on a free tier.'
findings.fix: State the free tier and the domain billing once (FAQ 3 answers the question directly); feature_5 and FAQ 4 add what is new.

findings.quote: A one-page site fits a business with one offer and one action a visitor should take
findings.issue: 'One action per page' is restated in howto_description 'Start with the one thing a visitor should do', FAQ 6 'The best one page websites keep one action in view', FAQ 10 'Each of these one page website examples has one main action.'
findings.fix: Say it once (howto_step_1); FAQ 6 can describe what the best ones in galleries share beyond that.

findings.quote: A new entry can also post to Slack or email whoever answers it.
findings.issue: Restated in howto_step_5_des 'a row in your database, an email to you, a Slack post for the large jobs'.
findings.fix: Keep the routing in howto_step_5; feature_3 can describe the row itself (fields, status, export).
